subject: Fwd: Request: no-train commitment + subprocessors and cross-border evidence
messages:
From: Ruth Alvarez <r.alvarez@fidelityhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: no-train commitment + subprocessors and cross-border evidence

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Fidelity Health is excited about the prospect of Redwood powering our clinical note summarization pilot. Before procurement can move forward we need confirmation on a few privacy points from legal/compliance: 

- Can Redwood commit to a no-training/no-model-improvement use of fidelity data (application-only) and include that explicitly in the DPA or an addendum?
- If a full no-train commitment is not feasible, what are the precise opt-out controls we can toggle (and how are they enforced operationally)?
- We need the current list of subprocessors and a short attestation that none have access to raw prompt/response content used in the pilot.
- Clarify international data transfer safeguards: our data team requires detail on transfer mechanisms for backups, logging, or any model telemetry.
- Expected timeline for a signed DPA and any procurement redlines (we're aiming for contract execution by end of February).

Can you point me to the DPA draft and any supporting attestation docs? Happy to loop in procurement as needed (procurement@fidelityhealth.com).

Best,
Ruth
Director, Vendor Risk Management
Fidelity Health

--
Attachment: pilot-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet listing models & data categories)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ruth Alvarez <r.alvarez@fidelityhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: no-train commitment + subprocessors and cross-border evidence

Hi Ruth — great to hear from you and really glad the demo was helpful.

High-level answers up front:
- We can offer a contractual no-training/no-improvement commitment for customer-supplied input/outputs for specific workloads (pilot scope) — this is implemented as a config + DPA addendum and enforced by routing and storage controls.
- If you need a broader opt-out, we have an "opt-out for model improvement" workflow (per-account flag + audit logs). Operational enforcement includes separate queues, disabled telemetry collection, and retention rules.
- Ive attached the DPA draft and a recent subprocessor attestation PDF. The attestation lists subprocessors and their access levels; the attestation also includes a statement that subprocessors do not use customer conversational content for model training unless explicitly agreed.
- Cross-border: we support SCCs and standard contractual mechanisms; for backups and logs we can restrict geography and provide supplemental SOC2 evidence on controls.

Ive looped in Lauren (Legal) and Marcus (Solutions) to confirm the textual commitments and production evidence. Marcus/Lauren — could you review the attached DPA redline and the attestation and suggest a one-paragraph no-train addendum we can send Ruth today? Ruth, Ill also share a short opt-out template if you prefer that route.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood to share DPA redline + attestation (attached).
2) Fidelity to confirm whether they prefer a strict no-train DPA addendum or the opt-out flag approach.
3) Procurement to review and return any commercial redlines (DocuSign link once agreed).

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: FidelityHealth-DPA-draft.pdf, subprocessor-attestation-2027.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: no-train commitment + subprocessors and cross-border evidence

Tessa / team — quick legal take:

1) No-train addendum: we can propose language that restricts model improvement for the defined pilot dataset (we should reference the pilot-scope.xlsx to keep it narrow). Suggested one-liner: "Redwood will not use Customer Data (including prompts, completions, and derived embeddings) to train, improve or update Redwood models or any third-party models during the Term, except as explicitly agreed in writing."

2) Operational enforcement & evidence: propose we provide the following bundle to Fidelity: DPA redline, subprocessor attestation (signed), system design note summarizing separate ingestion pipeline + disabled telemetry, and a short SOC2 control extract for logging/storage controls.

3) Subprocessors: current set includes managed cloud infra partner (us-west region), S3-compatible object storage provider (data-at-rest), and an observability vendor for metrics (no access to content). We must not list raw internal vendors beyond the attestation PDF.

4) Cross-border transfers: we can offer SCCs and the option to pin storage and backups to US regions only. If they need on-prem or VPC-private deployment, Redwood Private is an option (we should flag cost/time).

Marcus — can you confirm the timeline for preparing the system-design note and the opt-out template? Karthik — need a 1-paragraph attestation signoff we can include in the bundle.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
